To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a human mAb against the mannose endocytic receptor was used to target a human tumor Ag to DCs and to induce a potent anti-tumor T cell response.
the targeting of tumor Ag to DCs by the mannose receptor can generate both CD8 and CD4 T cell responses.
a fully human mAb to the mannose receptor can be used to target soluble tumor Ag into human DCs resulting in their efficient presentation in the context of multiple HLA molecules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel approach to cancer vaccine development.
the development of novel immunotherapies for cancer and infectious diseases.
the generation of human fusion proteins that target tumor Ag to DCs for the induction of potent Ag-specific T cell immunity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the specific targeting of tumor Ags to DCs via endocytic receptors is a promising approach for cancer immunotherapy.
targeting the mannose receptor on human DCs provides a means for the delivery of a variety of tumor Ags for efficient T cell priming and activation.
the targeting of tumor Ags to the human mannose receptor on DCs provides a means for the generation of potent anti tumor immune responses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the specific targeting of exogenous soluble tumor Ag to the mannose receptor on human DCs results in the generation of multiple Ag specific T cell populations.
we are able to target a tumor Ag to human DCs using a fully human mAb that is internalized by receptor mediated endocytic mechanisms.

we have shown that the mannose receptor is a viable target for Ag delivery to DCs, that it is possible to generate human mAbs to this receptor, and that these can be used to deliver tumor Ag for the generation of Ag specific T cell immune responses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mannose receptor can be used to target Ags to human DCs and that these targeted Ags can then be processed and presented to CD4 and CD8 T cells in the context of a variety of HLA molecules.
targeting Ags to DCs through the mannose receptor can lead to the presentation of Ags by multiple HLA molecules.
we have shown that the human mannose receptor can be used as a targeting mechanism to deliver tumor Ag to DCs.
